name: Law and Gospel in the Pentateuch

objectives.text: Identify a command God gave and a promise God made in a Bible story from the books of Moses
Recall that God rescued Israel from Egypt before he gave them the Ten Commandments
State that no one except Jesus keeps all of God's commands perfectly
Retell God's first promise of a Savior after Adam and Eve disobeyed his command
Name Jesus as the one who obeyed God's law perfectly in the place of his people
Describe how God forgave and restored Israel after they broke his law with the golden calf
Explain how God's law works like a mirror that shows people their sin
Summarize the whole law in the two great commandments taken from Deuteronomy and Leviticus
Explain how the animal sacrifices pointed to God providing a substitute to bear the penalty for sin
Explain from the story of Abraham that God counted him righteous because he believed God's promise
Compare trying to earn God's favor by obedience with trusting God's promise, using God's words to Israel about why he chose them
Interpret the bronze serpent as a picture of salvation that comes by looking in faith to what God provides
Distinguish the moral, ceremonial, and civil laws of the Pentateuch using examples of each
Explain why the Reformed tradition teaches that the law guides the grateful life of the redeemed and is not a way to earn salvation
Analyze the three uses of the law as the Reformed tradition confesses them, showing how the law convicts, restrains, and guides
Interpret Paul's description of the law as a guardian that held God's people until Christ came
Trace how Deuteronomy anticipates Israel's failure to keep the law and promises a circumcised heart fulfilled in the New Covenant
Explain how Paul uses texts from Leviticus and Deuteronomy to show that the law demands perfect obedience and pronounces a curse that Christ bore
Explain how the Pentateuch administers the covenant of grace through promises, sacrifices, and types that foreshadow Christ
Explain the relationship between the covenant of works with Adam and the covenant of grace announced after the fall
Construct a law and gospel reading of a Pentateuch passage that distinguishes its commands from its promises and shows how each points to Christ
Compare the Reformed and Lutheran accounts of law and gospel, especially their treatment of the law's use in the believer's life
Evaluate the errors of legalism and antinomianism using the Pentateuch and Paul's teaching on the law
Defend the Reformed position that believers in both Testaments are saved by grace through faith in the one Mediator
Synthesize how the Torah as a whole bears witness to Christ through its commands, promises, and patterns

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (identifying law and gospel, inability to keep the law, Christ's obedience, forgiveness, the law as mirror, sacrifices, works versus trust, the law as guide, three uses, the guardian of Galatians 3, New Covenant, grace in the Old Testament, law and gospel hermeneutics, legalism and antinomianism, continuity of salvation, Torah as witness to Christ). Anchored each in Pentateuch texts rather than only New Testament ones. Recast 'Observe that God forgives us' as describing God's restoration of Israel after the golden calf. Added grace preceding law at Sinai, the first gospel promise, the two great commandments, Abraham justified by faith, God's unmerited choice of Israel, the bronze serpent, moral, ceremonial, and civil law, Paul's use of Leviticus 18:5 and Deuteronomy 27:26, covenant of works and grace, and a Reformed and Lutheran comparison. Corrected confession citations to full names and added Westminster Larger Catechism Q96 and Q97 alongside Q95 for the uses of the law.
